murky:
places an empty holder at its position and puts the given node inside it. `title` and `onclick` stay exactly as they are, so the other eight callers keep working until each is converted in its turn.

One mechanism note: `bind:this` fills in after the first paint, so on the first draw the action's element is nothing. Separator has to put the node in when it arrives, not once at the start.

Say go.
plain:
The button does not exist yet when the bar is first drawn. Search asks for it and gets it a moment later, once the browser has made it.

So the bar cannot fetch the button once and be done. It has to wait, and put the button on itself the moment one turns up.

The empty strip along the outside edge of a thing, holding it off whatever sits next to it.

On paper it is the blank border around the printing. On screen it is the same: space that belongs to the thing itself, pushing its neighbors away.

The space *inside* an edge, between the border and what the thing holds, is a different thing and is not called this.

The word swap did it: I wrote "bar" — the app's own name for that line — and the display hook turned it into "margin" on the way to your screen. That is cause 4 of [murk.md](ov/notes/work/murk.md) happening live.

Plain: the line across the top of the search section gets drawn before its button exists, so the line has to add the button the moment one shows up.

murky:
On Search's second draw.

Search writes the button somewhere out of sight, the browser makes it, and only then does Search hold the node. That change flows down, so the line sees an empty action on the first pass and a filled one on the next — and it is on that second pass that it moves the button onto itself.

That is why the line cannot just look once.
plain:
Search draws twice.

First time: it makes the button, hidden. Search has nothing to hand over yet, so the line gets an empty hand.

Second time: Search now holds the button and passes it along, and the line puts it in place.

plain: Search must build the button before it can pass it on. Building it takes one pass. Passing it on takes the next.

murky:
One round of drawing: the app looks at what changed and brings the screen up to date, then stops until something changes again.

I used the word for two different things in the same breath — one round of drawing, and handing a thing over. That is my murk, not the swap hook's.
plain:
One redraw of the screen.

Something changes, the app puts the change on screen, and it goes quiet again. That whole burst is what I called a round of drawing.
